IS : 2000 ( Part 5 ) - 1985 

Indian Standard 

METHODS OF 
CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF BAUXITE 

PART 5 DETERMINATION OF TITANIA 

(First Revision) 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 5 ) ( First Revision ) was adopted by 
the Indian Standards Institution on 24 December 1985, after the draft 
finalized by the Methods of Chemical Analysis of Ores, Minerals and 
Refractories Sectional Committee had been approved by the Structural 
and Metals Division Council. 

0.2 IS : 2000-1962* which covered determination of loss on ignition, total 
silica, non-reactive and reactive silica; alumina; ferric oxide by dichromate 
method, permanganate and colorimetric methods; titania by reduction 
( volumetric ) and colorimetric methods; phosphorus; calcium oxide; 
magnesium oxide and manganous oxide was first published 
in 1962. While reviewing this standard the Sectional Commi- 
ttee felt the need for the revision of this standard. On the basis of 
experience gained during these years the committee decided to revise 
this standard into different parts covering determination of each element 
in a separate part, which on publication would supersede that element 
given in IS : 2000-1962*. This part covers determination of titania. 
The other parts are; 

Part 1 Determination of loss on ignition 

Part 2 Determination of silica ( Si02, 05 to 10*0 percent ) 

Part 3 Determination of alumina 

Part 4 Determination of ferric oxide 

Part 6 Determination of vanadium ( V < 0"1 percent ) 

part 7 Determination of phosphorus pentoxide ( P2O5 < 0*5 per- 
cent ) 

Part 8 Determination of manganous oxide ( MnO < 0*5 percent ) 

The procedures for determination of CaO and MgO in bauxite are at 
Present under investigation and will be given in subsequent parts. 

* Methods of chemical analysis of bauxite. 

3 



IS : 2000 ( Part 5 ) - 1985 

0.3 In this revision the reduction ( volumetric ) method has been deleted 
and colorimetric method has been substituted by spectrophotometric 

method. 

0.4 In preparation of this revision due consideration has been given to 
the facilities available in the country to carry out such analysis. 

0,5 In reporting the results of a test or analysis made in accordance 
with this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be 
rounded off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This Standard ( Part 5 ) covers the determination of titania in bauxite 
in the range of 0*5 to 12*0 percent. 

2. SAMPLING 

2.1 Sample shall be drawn and prepared as per the method prescribed 
in 2 of IS : 2000 ( Part 1 )- 19851". 

3. QUALITY OF REAGENTS 

3.1 Unless specified otherwise, analytical grade reagents and distilled 
water shall be employed in the test. 

4. DETERMINATION OF TITANIA BY THE SPECTROPHOTO- 
METRIC METHOD 

4.1 Outline of the Method — The yellow colour produced by hydrogen 
peroxide in sulphuric acid medium in presence of phosphoric acid is 
measured in a spectrophotometer. Amount of titania is evaluated from 
the titanium calibration curve obtained under the similar experimental 
condition. 

4.2 Reagents 

4.2.1 Dilute Sulphuric Acid — 1 : 1 ( v\v ). 

4.2.2 Dilute Phosphoric Acid — 1 : 3 ( vjv ). 

4.2.3 Hydrogen Peroxide — 20 percent by volume. 

4.2.4 Standard Titania Solution ( 1 ml = 1 mg of TiC>2 ) — Dissolve 
05 g of calcined titania in concentrated hydrofluoric acid in a platinum 
dish. Then add carefully 25 ml of concentrated sulphuric acid and 
heat to strong fumes to remove fluoride. Cool, dilute with water stirr- 
ing continuously and make up to 500 ml in a volumetric flask. 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 

fMethods of chemical analysis of bauxite: Parti Determination of loss on ignition 
( first revision ). 

4 



IS t 2000 ( Part 5 ) « 1985 

4.3 Procedure 

4.3.1 Take a suitable aliquot ( containing more than 0*5 mg Ti0 2 ) 
from the main solution [ see 5*3.3 of IS ; 2000 ( Part 2 )-1985* ] in a 100 ml 
volumetric flask add 10 ml of sulphuric acid, 1-2 ml of phosphoric acid 
and dilute to about 80 ml volume. Add about 3 ml of hydrogen per- 
oxide, shake to mix the solution. Make up to the mark with water. 
Measure the intensity of the colour after half-an-hour in a spectrophoto- 
meter at 425 nm in a suitable cell. 

4.3.2 A standard curve is prepared from 0, 0*5, 1, 2, 3 and 4 ml of 
standard titania solution in a 100-ml volumetric flask following the 
procedure as described in 4.3.1. 

4.4 Calculation 

Ti0 2 , percent — — - x 100

B = mass in mg of the sample taken.
